results.authors: Montalban X, Lebrun-Frenay C, Oh J, et al.
results.key_findings: Five regions for dissemination in space (periventricular, cortical/juxtacortical, infratentorial, spinal cord, optic nerve). The optic nerve can be shown by MRI, OCT or VEP. The kappa free light chain index is accepted alongside CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands. The central vein sign and paramagnetic rim lesions are supporting MRI markers.
results.title: Diagnosis of multiple sclerosis: 2024 revisions of the McDonald criteria

results.authors: Wattjes MP, Ciccarelli O, Reich DS, et al.
results.key_findings: Diagnostic MRI should include the brain with 3D FLAIR, T2 and pre- and post-gadolinium T1, and the spinal cord with at least two sagittal sequences, ideally in the same session.
results.title: 2021 MAGNIMS-CMSC-NAIMS consensus recommendations on the use of MRI in patients with multiple sclerosis

output.summary: The 2024 revision of the McDonald criteria (Montalban et al., Lancet Neurol 2025) adds the optic nerve as a fifth region, accepts the kFLC index as an alternative to oligoclonal bands, and allows the central vein sign and paramagnetic rim lesions as supporting markers. Lesions in four or five regions establish dissemination in space without a separate test of dissemination in time; with two or three regions, dissemination in time, positive CSF or the central vein sign is needed. In people over 50 or with vascular risk factors, additional supporting evidence is recommended.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not diagnose MS based on non-specific white-matter lesions alone without meeting the 2024 revised McDonald criteria and excluding mimics
Do not use chronic oral corticosteroids as maintenance treatment for MS: they do not prevent relapses or disability and cause cumulative harm
Do not administer live-attenuated vaccines after initiation of B-cell depleting therapy (ocrelizumab, ofatumumab) or S1P modulators (fingolimod, ozanimod)
Do not omit spinal cord MRI in a patient with myelopathic signs even if the brain MRI alone meets DIS: cord lesions count toward DIS and separate MS from NMOSD
required_recommendations: State relapsing-remitting MS by the 2024 McDonald criteria, naming the regions that give DIS and, where needed, what gives DIT or positive CSF (here periventricular, juxtacortical, infratentorial, spinal cord and right optic nerve: five regions, so no separate DIT is required).

Exclude urinary tract infection (urinalysis and culture) before steroids, then give high-dose methylprednisolone for the disabling relapse (right optic neuritis 20/80 with spastic paraparesis and incontinence): IV 1 g daily for 3-5 days as an inpatient or oral 500 mg daily for 5 days; consider plasma exchange if severe deficits do not respond.

Offer disease-modifying therapy after diagnosis, choosing efficacy by disease activity (concurrent optic neuritis and myelitis, enhancing brain, optic nerve and cord lesions, lesions in 5 of 5 regions).

Before starting disease-modifying therapy, check full blood count with lymphocyte count, liver function, HBsAg and anti-HBc, hepatitis C and VZV IgG (HIV already non-reactive), and give any live vaccine at least 4-6 weeks before treatment starts
Measure the post-void residual for the urgency and incontinence: offer an antimuscarinic if the residual is low, and intermittent self-catheterisation if it is above 100 mL.
Make sure the iron deficiency anaemia of an adult man (Hb 10.9 g/dL, MCV 77.6 fL) has been investigated for a gastrointestinal source, arranging upper and lower endoscopy if it has not.

key_clinical_evidence: Ten days of painful right optic neuritis (acuity 20/80, right RAPD, colour desaturation, pain on adduction, normal disc) with an enhancing swollen 15 mm retrobulbar segment of the right optic nerve and a prolonged right P100 (121 ms).

Concurrent myelopathy: spastic paraparesis worse on the right, bilateral Babinski signs and clonus, urgency with incontinence and Lhermitte sign, matched by the C3-C4 dorsal and right lateral column lesion and the left lateral-column T6-T7 lesion.

DIS: 5 of 5 regions: periventricular (ovoid lesions, two enhancing), juxtacortical (left frontal, right parietal), infratentorial (both middle cerebellar peduncles), spinal cord (C3-C4, T6-T7), optic nerve (right). With five regions no separate DIT or CSF is needed; enhancing and non-enhancing lesions also coexist.
Earlier episode 8 months ago: 3 weeks of left arm and hand numbness, never evaluated.
AQP4-IgG and MOG-IgG negative by cell-based assay, short peripheral cord lesions and five CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands (kFLC index 31.6) argue against NMOSD and MOGAD.
Microcytic anaemia (Hb 10.9 g/dL, MCV 77.6 fL) is his known iron deficiency on treatment; it does not explain the neurological picture.

patient.history_present_illness: This 36-year-old right-handed man presents to the neurology service after being admitted through the emergency department with a 10-day history of progressive, painful vision loss in his right eye accompanied by worsening bilateral leg weakness. The visual symptoms began as a dull, aching pain behind his right eye that worsened with eye movements, followed two days later by progressive blurring of vision in that eye. Over the ensuing week, his vision continued to deteriorate to the point where he can no longer read print with the right eye. He also noticed that colors appeared washed out and dull when viewed through the affected eye compared to the left. Concurrently, he developed increasing heaviness and stiffness in both legs, making it difficult to climb stairs or run, activities he previously performed without difficulty. He reports two episodes of urinary urgency over the past week, once resulting in incontinence, which he found deeply distressing and out of character. He also describes an unusual electric shock-like sensation radiating down his spine and into his legs whenever he bends his neck forward, which began approximately five days ago. Upon further questioning, he recalls an episode approximately eight months ago in which his left arm and hand became numb and tingled for about three weeks before gradually resolving on its own. He did not seek medical attention at that time, attributing it to a pinched nerve from sleeping in an awkward position. He also notes that his symptoms seem to worsen after hot showers or during exercise, with his vision becoming more blurry and his legs feeling heavier in the heat. He denies any recent illness, fever, headache, seizures, difficulty swallowing, or bowel dysfunction. He has no history of rashes, joint pains, oral ulcers, or sicca symptoms. He has not traveled recently and denies any tick exposure.

neurological_exam.additional: Uhthoff phenomenon reported by patient: symptoms worsen after hot showers or exercise. Lhermitte sign reproducible on examination. Right relative afferent pupillary defect clearly demonstrable with swinging flashlight test.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose testing intact bilaterally without dysmetria. Heel-to-shin mildly impaired on the right with subtle ataxia. Rapid alternating movements normal in upper extremities.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: CN II: Visual acuity reduced in the right eye to 20/80 with Snellen chart (left eye 20/20). Right relative afferent pupillary defect (Marcus Gunn pupil) present. Color desaturation on the right (red appears washed out). Fundoscopic exam shows normal optic discs bilaterally, with no swelling or pallor. CN III-VI: Extraocular movements full bilaterally, mild pain with right eye adduction noted. No nystagmus. CN V: Facial sensation intact to light touch and pinprick in all divisions bilaterally. CN VII: Face symmetric, no weakness. CN VIII: Hearing intact to finger rub bilaterally. CN IX-XII: Palate elevates symmetrically, gag intact, tongue midline, sternocleidomastoid and trapezius full strength.
neurological_exam.gait: Gait mildly spastic with circumduction noted bilaterally, more prominent on the right. Tandem gait impaired with tendency to veer to the right. Romberg sign positive.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented to person, place, time, and situation. Speech fluent without dysarthria or paraphasic errors. Attention intact; serial sevens performed accurately. Short-term memory intact, recalling 3/3 objects at 5 minutes. No evidence of cognitive impairment on bedside assessment.
neurological_exam.motor: Bulk normal throughout. Tone mildly increased in bilateral lower extremities with subtle spasticity at the knees. Strength: upper extremities 5/5 bilaterally in all muscle groups. Lower extremities: hip flexion 4+/5 bilaterally, knee extension 4+/5 bilaterally, ankle dorsiflexion 5/5 bilaterally. No pronator drift.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 2+ bilaterally, triceps 2+ bilaterally, brachioradialis 2+ bilaterally. Patellar 3+ bilaterally (brisk). Achilles 3+ bilaterally. Plantar responses extensor (upgoing) bilaterally (positive Babinski sign). Unsustained ankle clonus (4-5 beats) bilaterally.
neurological_exam.sensory: Decreased vibration sense at bilateral great toes (diminished compared to medial malleoli). Light touch intact throughout. Pinprick intact. Proprioception intact in fingers and toes. Lhermitte sign present: flexion of the neck produces electric shock-like sensation radiating down the spine and into the legs.
